rows.theme: Counterexample to a force–time definition of work
rows.scenarioAndRequiredInterpretation: Two trials deliberately match force and elapsed time while changing path; distinguish a correct work unit from a proposed competing rule.
rows.distractorReasoningDomains: Force-only prediction; force-time product; irrelevant missing mass.
rows.changeAndCollisionJudgment: Keeps the work-unit/force-time misconception. Replaces a definition-completion question with a two-trial counterexample: the proposed rule predicts equality, while the taught rule predicts unequal work. The learner must interpret what the paired observations disprove; the complete paired stimulus is absent from the definition guide. Parallel application of taught work, not an independent outcome.

rows.theme: Work along a route that changes direction

rows.changeAndCollisionJudgment: Keeps formula applicability and direction. Replaces an omitted-direction record with explicitly changing path/force directions and asks whether local valid applications can be summed. Unlike the straight-path guide, the decision requires distinguishing local alignment from one fixed global direction and route length from endpoint distance. No angle/cosine or signed-work law introduced.

rows.theme: Lifting after part of a load is set down

rows.theme: Power from a clock reset record
rows.scenarioAndRequiredInterpretation: Interpret two elapsed readings around a reset before selecting the denominator belonging to the full work.
rows.distractorReasoningDomains: Subtracting readings across a reset; retaining only one segment.
rows.changeAndCollisionJudgment: Keeps correct association of work and elapsed time. A timer reset changes the observation model: add two elapsed readings rather than subtract two readings on one clock. U03-S03-M04 already teaches counter-reset accounting; U03-S08-M04 teaches adding uncounted elapsed time to a clock reading. These are strong shared procedures, not new reasoning. The stimulus now requires interpreting two time segments around a reset and diagnosing an invalid subtraction before associating work with that duration. Restrict as a parallel candidate, not independent form capacity.

rows.scenarioAndRequiredInterpretation: Accept a correct whole-interval mean while rejecting a contradictory claim that power stayed constant throughout.
rows.distractorReasoningDomains: Mean implies constant rate; using only an endpoint segment for the whole interval.
rows.changeAndCollisionJudgment: Keeps average-versus-constant power. The original merely lacked subinterval evidence; the revision provides observations that contradict constancy while preserving a correct whole-interval mean. The learner must accept one part of a claim and refute another using equal-duration work totals. Mean-speed dependencies are retained; no claim of instant-by-instant reconstruction.

rows.theme: Unknown scale of a duration increase
rows.scenarioAndRequiredInterpretation: Determine whether the direction of a rate change follows when work doubles but elapsed-time growth is unspecified.
rows.distractorReasoningDomains: Work-only increase; time-only decrease; assuming both changes cancel.
rows.changeAndCollisionJudgment: Keeps joint work/time scaling. Replaces specified scale factors with an unspecified increase and asks what is identifiable. Three admissible durations demonstrate all orderings; this is not a disguised number change in a ratio calculation. S03-D01 is the complementary identifiable-order case and must be recorded as a dependent pair for later form design.

rows.scenarioAndRequiredInterpretation: Find a common observation time when two accumulated works agree, using different elapsed times for the machines.
rows.distractorReasoningDomains: Power implies immediate lead; same duration for unequal starts; early start guarantees a permanent lead.
rows.changeAndCollisionJudgment: Keeps the distinction between larger power and larger completed work. Must associate different elapsed durations with a common observation time and test equality, not equate power with total work. Related motion/time comparisons remain explicit dependencies; no new motion law required.

rows.scenarioAndRequiredInterpretation: Check two operating modes against both explicit limits; equal calculated powers can mask a violation of the separate force limit.
rows.distractorReasoningDomains: Checking only power; inventing a speed limit; combining alternative modes.
rows.changeAndCollisionJudgment: Keeps force-speed power and device capability. Replaces one power ceiling with two explicitly supplied simultaneous constraints; equal power in both modes conceals a force-limit violation in only one. Rejects assuming a new speed limit or summing mutually exclusive modes. Both restrictions are scenario data, not a new mechanical law.

rows.scenarioAndRequiredInterpretation: Combine each record’s mass, lifting distance and time, then identify the record inconsistent with the common power of the others.
rows.distractorReasoningDomains: Choosing a row from only height, mass or duration.
rows.changeAndCollisionJudgment: Keeps comparing lifting power. Requires matching all three columns and finding the inconsistent record. Repeated mgh/t procedure is declared parallel capacity, not new reasoning coverage.
